Tree planting at Itierio Comprehensive School
Tree planting at Nyabiosi Comprehensive School
Acknowledgment of Partners

Kisii University gratefully acknowledges the generous support rendered by its partners in this noble cause. Special appreciation goes to Equity Bank and Safaricom Foundation which have supported the university through the donation of thousands of tree seedlings and subsequent engagement in joint tree planting activities. This powerful synergy between academia and the private sector has yielded visible results, turning previously bare landscapes into flourishing green belts. Such collaborations demonstrate that meaningful environmental action is possible when institutions unite for a common purpose.
Tree planting with equity bank at Riamaoncha Comprehensive School

Let us remember that the tree we plant today is a lecture we give to the future. Kisii University is proud to be a green arrow on Kenya’s compass, pointing toward a sustainable, resilient, and prosperous tomorrow.
Join us. Plant a tree. Secure the future.
innovation_report: KISII UNIVERSITY’S INNAUGURAL INNOVATION WEEK: CO-CREATING A SUSTAINABLE FUTURE
April 7–10, 2026 | New Auditorium, Kisii University

Kisii University made history in April 2026, hosting its first-ever Innovation Week, a bold declaration of its transformation from a traditional teaching institution into an innovation-driven university. Under the theme “Co-creating a Sustainable Future Through Interdisciplinary Research, Green Innovation and Community Impact,” the four-day event brought together over 300 participants, 97 innovations, and 19 partner institutions from across Kenya.
A New Chapter for Kisii University

In his opening remarks, Vice-Chancellor Prof. Nathan Ogechi declared, “We cannot wait for perfect conditions to innovate; we must start with what we have, even if small.” He outlined the University’s strategic shift over the next three to five years, highlighting milestones such as training over 30 staff in intellectual property management, registering 13 innovations with the Kenya Copyright Board, and enrolling in KeNIA’s Commercialisation Support Programme.
Keynotes That Inspired Action

Prof. James Njiru, CEO of AICAD, called for stronger academia-industry-community linkages, urging researchers to align their work with practical needs. “Research disconnected from real-world application risks limited impact,” he cautioned.

Dr. Tony Omwansa, CEO of Kenya National Innovation Agency (KeNIA), addressed the notorious “Valley of Death” in innovation, the funding gap between idea and prototype. He encouraged Kisii University to consistently produce at least four viable start-ups annually, positioning graduates as job creators.
The Green Silicon Savannah Vision

Jeremy Riro the CEO of Fie_Labs Innovation Hub electrified the final day, unveiling a vision to transform South Western Kenya into a “Green Silicon Savannah” within 3–5 years. He championed the WEFE Nexus (Water-Energy-Food-Ecosystem) powered by Artificial Intelligence, noting that Africa’s vulnerability to climate change is actually its greatest innovation opportunity. “That farmer needs systems, technology, and partnerships, not sympathy,” he urged.
Innovations That Shine

Of the 89 innovations exhibited, standout projects included Kenya Watch AI (Overall Winner) by first-year student Douglas Mwebi, Banana Hair & Vegan Leather, MediBot, NeuroBridge, and Eco-Bricks from Plastic Waste. Kisii University dominated software and AI categories, while Kisii National Polytechnic excelled in hardware prototypes—revealing a powerful complementary synergy.
Partnerships and Resource Mobilization

The University appreciates our partners including KMFRI, Gusii Mwalimu SACCO, Elite Savers CBO and Chip Globe International. The official launch of Club Innovate, a student-led enterprise, ensures the momentum continues beyond the week.
Looking Ahead

The inaugural Innovation Week proved that Kisii University is no longer just a consumer of knowledge but a producer of solutions. As Prof. Ogechi put it, the start may be small, but the trajectory is upward. With structured mentorship, strategic partnerships, and a growing pipeline of green innovations, Kisii University is poised to become the heartbeat of Africa’s sustainable future
Strategic Synergies: The Power of Partnership on innovation

Innovation rarely happens in isolation. True to this spirit, we are proud to announce Partnership on Innovation with the following institutions: Technical University of Mombasa, University of Eldoret, and Maasai Mara University.

As a testament to the strength of this collaboration, Kisii University actively participated in the Innovation Week hosted by the Technical University of Mombasa, University of Eldoret and Maasai Mara University.
Visit to the Kisii University stand by Prof. Shaukat Abdulrazak, Principal Secretary for State Department for Science, Research and Innovation in Kenya.

We are thrilled to share that during the hackathons held at the Technical University of Mombasa Innovation Week, our student innovators brought home exceptional recognition: Notably, our students emerged Number 1 and Number 5 overall out of over 16 competing teams

The first-place team was Aquaflow project presented by Aron Barbra from the School of Information Science and Technology. The solution aims to prevent fish mortality using AI and IoT for real-time monitoring and prediction. They were awarded Ksh 200,000 from Web3Clubs.

The fifth-place team was Exam Proctor engine presented by Davis Ogega from the School of Information Science and Technology. The invention addresses critical gaps in remote examination integrity by providing comprehensive monitoring capabilities that operate effectively across device types while maintaining user privacy and data security. They were awarded Ksh. 25,000 from Web3Clubs.

In addition to these rankings, our students (Ms.Aron Barbra and Mr.Douglas Mwebi , (a first year student who presented an AI-powrewered mental wellness platform) were awarded paid internships at a Web3clubs Foundation Limited , providing them with hands-on experience in cutting-edge blockchain and decentralized technologies.
This milestone not only highlights the caliber of our students but also demonstrates the power of cross-university collaboration in creating real-world opportunities.
We extend our deepest gratitude to our partner institutions and look forward to even greater achievements in the future.
The Dreamers & Doers: Meet the Innovators

At Kisii University, brilliant students and dedicated faculty are turning bold ideas into real-world solutions, thanks to their creativity, technical skill, and relentless drive. From lab benches to field tests, these dreamers and doers have worked tirelessly to develop innovations that tackle pressing problems, placing the university at the forefront of campus-led change. With the right support and unwavering determination, each of the visionaries below has proven that transformative ideas can become tangible reality. We extend our deepest applause and gratitude for their outstanding contributions, proof that the future is being built right here, right now.
Your Turn to Spark: Notice for the Upcoming Neil Campus Spark Challenge
Have you been sitting on an idea that could change the world? Now is your time to act.
The Office of Research Extension Innovation and Resource Mobilization hereby issues a formal Notice for the Upcoming Neil Campus Spark Challenge.

The Neil Campus Spark Challenge isn't just for students, it's for every member of our university community with a spark of ingenuity. Whether you're in a lecture hall, a lab, or a faculty office, if you have an idea that can transform healthcare, sustainability, or education, we want you on board.
Deadline: Registration closes on 30th May 2026.
Let the universe of ideas meet the power of action. We can’t wait to see what you build.

seed_programs.name: Climate-Resilient Agrifood Systems Program
seed_programs.summary: Coordinated research that strengthens climate resilience, productivity, and nutrition across agrifood value chains in Nyamira and neighbouring counties.
seed_programs.description: Improve climate resilience, productivity, and nutrition across crop, livestock, and fish value chains through integrated research and innovation.
seed_programs.objectives: Smallholder farmers face rising climate risks and market pressures that threaten food security and income across Western Kenya.
seed_programs.methodology: Co-design solutions with farmers and partners; test in real-world conditions; scale proven innovations; and inform policy and practice.
seed_programs.expected_outcomes: Higher yields and incomes, reduced climate risks, improved nutrition, and stronger value chain competitiveness.

seed_programs.name: Carbon Literacy for Youth Employability and Job Creation

seed_programs.description: Kisii University collaborates with Sheffield Hallam University, Durban University of Technology, Ladoke Akintola University of Technology, and Innovate Durban.
seed_programs.objectives: Localize and trans-create carbon literacy training, build green innovation skills, and improve youth employability.

seed_programs.name: Responsible Computing Challenge
seed_programs.summary: Mozilla Foundation supported responsible computing and ethical AI curriculum project.
seed_programs.description: Kisii University partners with Mozilla Foundation to embed ethical computing and responsible AI into computing science courses.
seed_programs.objectives: Train faculty and students on data privacy, cybersecurity, algorithmic bias, responsible AI, and ethical technology practice.

seed_projects.title: Climate-Smart Agriculture for Smallholder Food Security
seed_projects.summary: Improving productivity and food security through climate-smart agriculture technologies.
seed_projects.abstract: Farmer field trials test drought-tolerant crops, soil health practices, advisory services, and extension models.
seed_projects.objectives: Increase adoption of climate-smart practices among smallholder farmers.
seed_projects.methodology: Demonstration plots, farmer learning groups, extension visits, and seasonal monitoring.
seed_projects.expected_outcomes: Improved yields, stronger soil health, better farm decisions, and reduced climate vulnerability.
seed_projects.impact: Supports stable food supply and household income in Nyamira and neighbouring counties.

seed_projects.title: Agroforestry for Landscape Restoration
seed_projects.summary: Restoring farms and landscapes through agroforestry, tree nurseries, and soil conservation practices.
seed_projects.abstract: Community nurseries and farm-level tree integration are used to improve landscape resilience.
seed_projects.objectives: Improve soil protection, farm biodiversity, and long-term climate resilience.
seed_projects.methodology: Participatory farm planning, nursery establishment, field days, and survival monitoring.
seed_projects.expected_outcomes: More trees on farms, reduced erosion, stronger biodiversity, and improved microclimates.
seed_projects.impact: Creates resilient landscapes that support production and ecosystem services.

seed_projects.title: Climate Information Services for Farmers
seed_projects.summary: Delivering weather and agronomic information that helps farmers make timely production decisions.
seed_projects.abstract: Seasonal advisories, SMS updates, and extension clinics are co-produced with local partners.
seed_projects.objectives: Improve access to usable climate information for farmers and extension workers.
seed_projects.methodology: Advisory co-design, dissemination pilots, farmer feedback loops, and uptake analysis.
seed_projects.expected_outcomes: Better planting decisions, improved risk planning, and increased use of climate advisories.
seed_projects.impact: Reduces production losses caused by rainfall variability and delayed decisions.

seed_projects.title: Postharvest Loss Reduction Innovations
seed_projects.summary: Testing storage, handling, and market-linkage innovations that reduce postharvest losses.
seed_projects.abstract: Farmer groups test practical postharvest handling methods for grains, horticulture, and priority value chains.
seed_projects.objectives: Reduce losses between farm gate and market while improving quality and farmer returns.
seed_projects.methodology: Technology pilots, market assessments, group training, and quality monitoring.
seed_projects.expected_outcomes: Lower losses, better quality, stronger market readiness, and improved incomes.
seed_projects.impact: Helps households retain more value from harvested produce.

seed_projects.title: Water Quality and Ecosystem Health in Nyamira
seed_projects.summary: Monitoring water quality and ecosystem health to protect livelihoods and agricultural productivity.
seed_projects.abstract: Water sampling and ecosystem assessments inform land-use recommendations and local stewardship.
seed_projects.objectives: Track priority water-quality indicators and promote ecosystem management practices.
seed_projects.methodology: Field sampling, watershed mapping, community reporting, and policy engagement.
seed_projects.expected_outcomes: Cleaner water systems, improved stewardship, and evidence for local decision-making.
seed_projects.impact: Protects water resources that sustain farms, households, and ecosystems.

seed_projects.title: Smart Soil Moisture Monitoring for Smallholders
seed_projects.summary: Deploying low-cost soil moisture sensing to guide irrigation and water-use decisions.
seed_projects.abstract: Field-tested devices and dashboards support smallholder irrigation scheduling.
seed_projects.objectives: Improve water productivity through affordable monitoring and farmer-friendly guidance.
seed_projects.methodology: Sensor prototyping, field validation, farmer training, and dashboard feedback.
seed_projects.expected_outcomes: More efficient water use, reduced crop stress, and practical digital advisory tools.
seed_projects.impact: Supports smarter water management for smallholder farms.

seed_projects.title: Carbon Literacy for Youth Employability and Job Creation
seed_projects.summary: A regional collaboration building carbon literacy, green innovation skills, and youth employability pathways.
seed_projects.abstract: The project designs carbon literacy modules, tests youth enterprise support models, and documents employability outcomes.
seed_projects.objectives: Develop training modules, support student innovation teams, and publish regional learning briefs.
seed_projects.expected_outcomes: Carbon literacy toolkit, employability evidence, student prototypes, and policy briefs.
seed_projects.impact: Improves youth readiness for green jobs and climate-aware entrepreneurship.

seed_projects.title: Responsible Computing Challenge
seed_projects.summary: Mozilla Foundation supported project embedding responsible computing and ethical AI in the Computer Science syllabus.
seed_projects.abstract: Faculty and students are trained to navigate data privacy, cybersecurity, algorithmic bias, and ethical technology practice.
seed_projects.objectives: Embed ethical computing practices into academic curricula and professional practice.
seed_projects.expected_outcomes: Curriculum integration, workshops, industry collaboration, and student responsible-computing projects.
seed_projects.impact: Shapes technology professionals who are skilled and aware of societal and environmental implications.

seed_projects.title: Ethical Artificial Intelligence Curriculum Project
seed_projects.summary: Ethical AI learning initiative reflected in official university research stories and student reflections.
seed_projects.abstract: The course links AI ethics with law, psychology, sociology, and interdisciplinary responsible-technology practice.
seed_projects.objectives: Support ethical AI learning, reflective practice, and responsible innovation among computing students.
seed_projects.expected_outcomes: Student reflections, responsible AI projects, and stronger ethical technology practice.
seed_projects.impact: Builds student confidence in questioning, designing, and applying AI responsibly.

seed_success_stories.title: From low yields to stable harvests
seed_success_stories.summary: Farmer field trials helped smallholder households adopt soil health practices, timely advisories, and climate-smart planting decisions.
seed_success_stories.challenge: Smallholder farmers in Nyamira faced erratic rainfall, declining soil fertility, and limited access to practical climate information.
seed_success_stories.approach: The project worked with farmer groups, field schools, and extension teams to test soil amendments, water-wise practices, and advisory messages under real farm conditions.
seed_success_stories.outcomes: Participating farmers reported more reliable crop establishment, stronger soil management routines, and better confidence in seasonal decisions.
seed_success_stories.impact: The story demonstrates how program research translates into practical livelihood gains for households and extension networks.
seed_success_stories.future_directions: The team is expanding demonstration plots and packaging the lessons into farmer-facing training materials.
seed_success_stories.beneficiaries: Smallholder farmers, extension officers, and farmer field school groups.

seed_innovations_and_outputs.title: Smart Soil Moisture Sensor for Smallholder Farms
seed_innovations_and_outputs.summary: Low-cost IoT device for real-time soil moisture monitoring in smallholder farms.
seed_innovations_and_outputs.description: Field-tested prototype supporting irrigation decisions and water-use efficiency.
seed_innovations_and_outputs.problem_addressed: Farmers lack affordable, timely soil moisture information for irrigation and crop stress management.
seed_innovations_and_outputs.solution: Sensor kits connected to simple advisory dashboards and farmer-facing guidance.
seed_innovations_and_outputs.benefits: Improves irrigation timing, reduces water waste, and supports better crop performance.
seed_innovations_and_outputs.applications: Smallholder irrigation, demonstration farms, extension clinics, and student innovation projects.

seed_innovations_and_outputs.problem_addressed: Students need practical carbon literacy linked to employability and enterprise creation.
seed_innovations_and_outputs.solution: Short modules tied to local climate problems and business model development.
seed_innovations_and_outputs.benefits: Faster curriculum adoption, consistent assessment, and reusable training assets.
seed_innovations_and_outputs.applications: Student training, community workshops, enterprise incubation, and partner programmes.

seed_innovations_and_outputs.applications: Computer science teaching, student projects, industry workshops, and responsible AI learning.

seed_innovation_pathways.name: SoilSense Analytics
seed_innovation_pathways.summary: Venture pathway for deploying smart soil moisture monitoring support to smallholder farms.
seed_innovation_pathways.problem: Smallholder irrigation decisions are often made without timely soil moisture data.
seed_innovation_pathways.solution: Bundle low-cost sensors, advisory dashboards, and extension support into a deployable service.
seed_innovation_pathways.business_model: Device kits, maintenance support, and advisory subscriptions for farmer groups and partners.
seed_innovation_pathways.market: Smallholder irrigation schemes, demonstration farms, and county extension programmes.
seed_innovation_pathways.traction: Field-tested prototype with CRASP-linked smallholder sites.
